name: Tsodilo
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2001.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “With one of the highest concentrations of rock art in the world, Tsodilo has been called the "Louvre of the Desert". Over 4,500 paintings are preserved in an area of only 10 km2 of the Kalahari Desert. The archaeological record of the area gives a chronological account of human activities and environmental changes over at least 100,000 years. Local communities in this hostile environment respect Tsodilo as a place of worship frequented by ancestral spirits.”

The Tsodilo Hills are rock art, rock shelters and caves in Botswana. Wikipedia says UNESCO listed them in 2001 for their religious and spiritual significance to local peoples and their record of human settlement over many millennia, and that over 4,500 rock paintings are estimated there.
There are four chief hills, known as Male, Female and Child plus an unnamed knoll. The highest is 1,400 metres above sea level and they stand about 40 km from Shakawe.
The article adds that the most famous of the San paintings, the Laurens van der Post panel, is named after the writer who first described them in his 1958 book The Lost World of the Kalahari.

gaps: The communities, including the Hambukushu and the San, for whom the hills are sacred: their own accounts are not in the article read here.
